summary: Melinda Rogers-Hixon and Martha Rogers, members of the family controlling Rogers Communications, are suing the company, saying they are excluded from board meetings and given redacted documents. Melinda alleges a "personal vendetta" by her brother, Chair Edward Rogers, who she says reneged on a near-complete settlement. The suit revives the feud that erupted in 2021, when Edward won control of the board in court.
one_line: Rogers sisters Melinda Rogers-Hixon and Martha Rogers sue Rogers Communications, alleging oppression and exclusion from board information by chairman Edward Rogers, reigniting a family power struggle.
key_facts: Melinda Rogers-Hixon and Martha Rogers filed a court petition arguing Rogers Communications has been "oppressive" to them.
Rogers-Hixon's Sept. 20 letter to CEO Tony Staffieri says she is the target of a "personal vendetta" by her older brother, Chair Edward Rogers, who reneged on a near-complete agreement.
The family's controlling stake in Rogers Communications is worth close to C$8 billion ($5.9 billion).
Rogers shares closed down 2.2% to C$53.07 in Toronto on news of the lawsuit and have dropped 16% this year.

In October 2021, Edward Rogers won a court battle against his sisters and mother for board control; five directors were fired and replaced by five of his allies, and CEO Joe Natale was replaced by Tony Staffieri.
In early 2022 the family shelved their disagreements to avoid negative publicity during the C$20 billion Shaw Communications takeover, which closed on April 3, 2023.
As part of the truce, the sisters agreed not to take part in board discussions on the Shaw deal because Rogers-Hixon's personal lawyer's firm also works for competitor Telus Corp.
Settlement talks after the Shaw closing collapsed last month, according to Rogers-Hixon's affidavit.
The sisters seek a court order to attend all board and committee meetings in full and receive the same information as other directors.
Rogers spokesperson Sarah Schmidt says the company protected information from a competitor and the sisters could have chosen a different lawyer.
Rogers' corporate governance committee is investigating the 2021 events to inform decisions about Rogers-Hixon's status as a director, per a letter signed by lead director Robert Gemmell.
Rogers-Hixon was apparently forced out as a director of Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment.
Edward Rogers, the only son of founder Ted Rogers, chairs the family trust, which gives him significant power over the company.
Loretta Rogers died in June 2022, and executives Alan Horn and Phil Lind, allies of Edward, died in 2023.
